subject.title: Provider key pools + bucket-aware cooldown/backoff on 429 (Gemini projects) to prevent retry storms

question: Should OpenClaw add a native generic provider key/profile quota-bucket routing contract for Gemini-style project quotas, and should it live in core provider/auth fallback rather than a sidecar or plugin seam?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config, auth-profile routing, cooldown scope, provider selection, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not invent the product boundary.

options.title: Design Generic Bucket Routing
options.body: Define an additive core/provider contract for quota-bucket metadata and cooldown state, then implement Gemini as one consumer while keeping current flat rotation as the default.

options.title: Fold Into Provider-Pool Tracker
options.body: Treat this as an acceptance criterion under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41135 and keep this issue only for Gemini project-bucket evidence.

options.title: Keep External For Now
options.body: Recommend the sidecar or plugin approach until maintainers decide native bucket routing is worth the new config and state surface.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Bucket Routing
recommendation.body: Define an additive core/provider contract for quota-bucket metadata and cooldown state, then implement Gemini as one consumer while keeping current flat rotation as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans provider/auth routing, config compatibility, and product boundary tradeoffs, and steipete is the strongest current routing candidate from adjacent source history.
